specific_task_changes.before: Conceptualization: Designed and refined the molecular docking workflow, including strategies for receptor comparison and exploratory mutation analysis. Took primary responsibility for the overall design of the molecular dynamics studies.
specific_task_changes.after: Conceptualization: Designed and refined the molecular docking workflow, including strategies for receptor comparison and exploratory mutation analysis. Took primary responsibility for the overall design of the molecular dynamics studies;

specific_task_changes.before: Investigation: Independently carried out the early molecular docking studies, including receptor comparisons and exploratory mutation analysis. Identified and corrected problems in receptor structure alignment and docking settings through structural inspection and input checks. specific_task_changes.after: Investigation: Independently carried out the early molecular docking studies, including receptor comparisons and exploratory mutation analysis. Identified and corrected problems in receptor structure alignment and docking settings through structural inspection and input checks. Worked with Ruoxi Yang on the later docking calculations and molecular dynamics simulation system preparation;

specific_task_changes.before: Data Curation: Worked with Ruoxi Yang to organize docking results, interaction fingerprint (IFP) data, cross-receptor residue mappings, and residue annotations, preparing structured datasets for comparative analysis and visualization.
specific_task_changes.after: Data Curation: Worked with Ruoxi Yang to organize docking results, interaction fingerprint (IFP) data, cross-receptor residue mappings, and residue annotations for comparative analysis.

specific_task_changes.before: Analysis: Developed supporting analysis tools with Ruoxi Yang and collaborated on the later docking analyses, comparing docking scores, predicted binding poses, and residue-level interaction patterns across receptors and structural models. Jointly analyzed molecular dynamics trajectories to characterize receptor conformational changes, ligand motion, and the persistence of receptor–ligand contacts.
specific_task_changes.after: Analysis: Developed analysis tools with Ruoxi Yang, compared docking scores, poses, and residue interactions, and jointly analyzed molecular dynamics trajectories for receptor and ligand motion and contact persistence.

specific_task_changes.before: Visualization: Prepared structural visualizations of docking poses and predicted receptor–ligand interactions, together with residue-level IFP plots to compare contact patterns and support interpretation of receptor–ligand recognition. Generated visualizations of molecular dynamics post-analysis results, including root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) profiles and residue-level contact statistics, to illustrate receptor and ligand motion and the temporal behavior of local interactions.
specific_task_changes.after: Visualization: Produced docking-pose visualizations, residue-level IFP plots, and molecular dynamics figures, including root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) profiles and contact statistics.

specific_task_changes.before: Writing: Documented the docking and molecular dynamics workflows, results, and their interpretation. Wrote and revised the content of the Model page for the team Wiki.
specific_task_changes.after: Writing: Documented docking and molecular dynamics methods, results, and interpretations, and wrote and revised the Wiki Model page.

new_sections.heading: AI tool use
new_sections.body: AI tools supported our literature research, dry-lab software development, protein structure prediction, writing, and visual communication. Team members defined the research questions, reviewed AI-assisted outputs, and decided how to use them in the project.

new_sections.heading: ChatGPT — OpenAI
new_sections.body:
**Models:** GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-5.6 Luna; GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6.1 Luna; GPT-6 Astra.

**Tasks:** Background Research, Software, Visualization, Writing

**Background Research:** Used ChatGPT to help locate project-related literature, explore relevant research topics, and organize background information. It supported the team in working through concepts and methods related to the biosensor and its computational studies; scientific statements and references were checked against original publications.

**Software:** Used ChatGPT extensively during dry-lab software development, with substantial portions of the code developed through AI assistance. Team members guided the intended methods, ran and tested the code, and reviewed relevant sections to assess whether the implementation matched the research objectives.

**Visualization:** Used ChatGPT to refine Wiki layouts, assist with writing and revising plotting code, and directly generate visual assets for Wiki presentation. Team members reviewed and tested the plotting code and ran it on real project data or outputs from the team’s computational workflows. They reviewed the resulting plots and adapted visual materials to the project’s scientific content and design. Directly AI-generated visual assets are labelled on the Wiki.

**Writing:** Team members supplied research text they had already written, together with outlines, experimental records, or notes. ChatGPT was used mainly to polish language, translate text, and organize the presentation of that content. The members responsible for each section checked the revised text against the underlying research and records to preserve scientific meaning and accurately describe the work performed.

new_sections.heading: Claude — Anthropic
new_sections.body:
**Models:** Claude Opus 4.7; Claude Opus 5; Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Fable 5.

**Tasks:** Wiki Coding, Writing

**Wiki Coding:** Used Claude to assist with writing Wiki code and identifying and fixing bugs. Team members reviewed and tested the resulting changes to check that they supported the intended page content and functionality.

**Writing:** Used Claude to translate text written by team members, standardize formatting, and improve grammar and readability. The relevant contributors reviewed the revised text to ensure that scientific terminology, meaning, and descriptions of the work remained accurate.

new_sections.heading: DeepSeek — DeepSeek-AI
new_sections.body:
**Models:** DeepSeek-V4; DeepSeek-V4.1.

**Tasks:** Background Research

Used DeepSeek to support the reading and interpretation of scientific literature and to develop background knowledge relevant to the project. Its explanations helped the team work through unfamiliar concepts, while original publications remained the basis for checking scientific statements and references.

new_sections.heading: Doubao — ByteDance
new_sections.body:
**Models:** Doubao-Seed-2.0; Doubao-Seed-2.1.

**Tasks:** Background Research

Used Doubao to assist with understanding scientific papers and reviewing project-related background information. Team members checked the resulting explanations against the source literature before using them in research discussions or written materials.

new_sections.heading: AlphaFold 3 — Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs
new_sections.body:
**Tasks:** Investigation, Analysis

**Structure prediction:** The team locally deployed AlphaFold 3 using model parameters released by Google DeepMind and the reference databases provided through the official setup workflow for GPCR structure prediction. The predicted structures were used in downstream molecular docking with AutoDock Vina and molecular dynamics simulations with GROMACS. Team members configured and ran the workflow and reviewed its outputs as part of the project’s computational work. Detailed parameters and the computational workflow are documented on our Wiki Model page, in our public GitHub repository, and in our team repository on the official iGEM GitLab.

new_sections.heading: Human review and responsibility
new_sections.body: Team leaders or advisors reviewed key interpretations and conclusions before inclusion in project materials. The team retained final responsibility for the methods, use of AI-assisted outputs, and accuracy and integrity of the submitted work.

new_sections.heading: iGEM & partner offers
new_sections.body:
The following table records our use of resources offered through iGEM and its partners, including how they supported the project or why they were not used.

| Offer | Used | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iGEM Distribution Kit | No | The kit did not contain materials suitable for the project’s wet-lab experiments. |
| IDT Partner Offer | No | The offer was not relevant to the project’s needs. |
| Twist Partner Offer | No | The offer was not relevant to the project’s needs. |
| GenScript Partner Offer | Yes | We used GenScript’s FLASH Gene offer to order CYP76AD5 (1,506 bp) and DOD (804 bp), codon-optimized for expression in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, with free gene synthesis and subcloning into pUC57. The constructs were intended for downstream cloning and experimental evaluation. |
| Anthropic Partner Offer | No | The offer/resource was unavailable in our region. |

We also used GenScript’s GenSmart™ Design tool to generate plasmid maps and visualize the arrangement of genetic elements in our constructs, supporting experimental planning and project documentation.

The Anthropic entry concerns access to the partner offer. Our use of Claude as an AI tool is documented separately under AI Tool Use.

new_sections.heading: External contributions
new_sections.body: External advisors contributed expertise on agricultural needs, nematode detection, and practical considerations for field use. Their feedback helped the team examine the project’s intended application and identify questions requiring further evaluation. Financial support is acknowledged separately below.

new_sections.heading: Yurong Yao
new_sections.body:
**Institution Type:** Academic
**Relationship to the Team:** External Advisor

**Project Guidance:** Provided feedback on the agricultural relevance of the nematode early-warning project, emphasizing affordable detection, simple operation, and the practical needs of vegetable growers.

**Technical Consultation:** Explained the capabilities and limitations of existing nematode identification methods. Advised on soil sampling, sample transport and storage, separate sample handling, and treatment before disposal, helping the team consider the full workflow surrounding detection.

new_sections.heading: Qian Liu
new_sections.body:
**Institution Type:** Academic
**Relationship to the Team:** External Advisor

**Project Guidance:** Advised the team to define early detection around pre-planting decisions and connect results to the intended crop and management needs. Discussed the scope and limitations of interpreting ascaroside signals as indicators of nematode presence or density.

**Technical Consultation:** Explained morphological and molecular identification approaches and highlighted sample representativeness, soil-matrix interference, negative controls, and cross-reactivity testing as important considerations for evaluating the proposed biosensor.

new_sections.heading: Zhihao Pang
new_sections.body:
**Institution Type:** Academic
**Relationship to the Team:** External Advisor

**Project Guidance:** Critically reviewed the proposed field-use scenario and encouraged the team to focus on portability, minimal equipment requirements, and simpler operating steps. Recommended gathering direct evidence from affected fields and feedback from intended users.

**Technical Consultation:** Identified soil background color and potentially different degradation rates of ascr#3 and ascr#18 as factors requiring evaluation. Raised concerns about the environmental release of engineered yeast, prompting consideration of safety alongside practical usability.

new_sections.heading: ExCell Bio
new_sections.body:
**Institution Type:** Industry
**Relationship to the Team:** Sponsor

**Financial Support:** Provided financial sponsorship to support the team’s iGEM project.
